chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
If you are greeted with a greeting, return with a better one; and if a hand of help is extended to you, reciprocate with what exceeds it, although the credit remains with the one who was first.

key_terms.لِلْبَادِئِ: for the one who initiates / the first one
key_terms.يُرْبِي عَلَيْهَا: exceeds it / is greater than it

ai.seo_question: How should one respond to a greeting or favor according to Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates the social ethic of *ihsan* (excellence) by instructing believers to reciprocate greetings and favors with something superior, thereby perpetuating a cycle of generosity. While the initiator retains the primary merit for breaking the ice, the responder is urged to outdo them, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the etiquette of *salam* and *ihsan*. This teaching underscores the spiritual value of proactive kindness in maintaining communal harmony and elevating individual character.
